question: For tree planting in Canadian forest restoration, how do planting-stock traits (seedling size, nursery fertilization, mycorrhizal inoculation) affect survival and growth, and how do competing vegetation and site preparation change that?
text: Seedling-size treatments increased growth with high certainty and survival with low certainty, nursery fertilization had mixed low-certainty growth effects and no survival evidence, and mycorrhizal inoculation had mixed moderate-certainty survival and growth effects. More competing vegetation decreased survival with high certainty but had mixed low-certainty growth effects, vegetation control increased growth with high certainty and had mixed low-certainty survival effects, and single-treatment site preparation had mixed high-certainty survival and growth effects, while combined treatments are kept separate.
